newsitem.title: USA: Columbia University sues health group over name.
newsitem.headline: Columbia University sues health group over name.

text.p: Columbia University filed a suit Friday against Columbia/HCA Healthcare Corp for infringement on its trademarked name.

Columbia University, an Ivy League school in Manhattan, wants Columbia/HCA to pay unspecified damages, and to stop using the Columbia name in connection with health services. It also wants the company to run corrective advertising, the suit filed in Manhattan U.S. District Court said.

Columbia/HCA, based in Nashville, Tennessee, did not return a request for comment. Columbia/HCA owns or manages more than 300 hospitals in 32 states, primarily those in the South and West, the complaint said.

The company was formed to operate two Texas hospitals in 1988, but since has grown quickly. Since July the health care company has been agressively marketing Columbia as a tradename, the complaint said.
By adopting Columbia as a trademark, the suit said, the health care company "acted in bad faith in an effort to misappropriate the (university's) outstanding reputation and good will."

The university, founded in 1754 as Kings College, took the Columbia name after the American Revolution. Its medical reputation dates back to that era, as Columbia was the first university in the colonies to grant a medical doctorate, the suit said.
In 1921 the University formed the first academic medical centre, Columbia-Presbyterian Medical Centre, by joining with Presbyterian Hospital, which was founded in 1868.

According to the suit, the health care company has renamed its Oklahoma Presbyterian facility "The Columbia Presbyterian Hospital" and its University Hospital in Tamarac, Florida, "The Columbia-University Hospital."
